newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Andres calms to tropical depression near Nicaragua.
newsitem.headline: Andres calms to tropical depression near Nicaragua.

text.p: Former Tropical Storm Andres, now downgraded to a tropical depression, was moving east at nine miles (15 km) per hour midday Friday on the Nicaragua coast, weather reports said.
The storm front has been creeping by Mexico and Guatemala parallel to the Pacific coast, and could hit ground in the early afternoon, Nicaraguan weather official Mauricio Rosales said.
"In a very strange switch of direction it is moving toward the east and in this erratic behavior we don't doubt it could touch Nicaraguan territory," Rosales told Reuters.
Andres was spotted at midday at 100 miles (160 km) west of the port of Corinto, Nicaragua.
Flights from Costa Rica to Managua, fishing in Nicaragua's Pacific waters and Nicaraguan domestic flights were suspended on Friday because of strong rains and cloudy skies.

"It was recommended that domestic flights and Pacific fishing be suspended. The (suspension of) flights from Costa Rica is because of visibility problems, but international flights were not suspended," weather official Milagros Castro said on the radio.
He estimated Andres would continue sending wind and rains over Nicaragua through the weekend.
Two children drowned in the rains in Managua this past week.
